skill.name: surgical-patch
skill.description: Fix bugs and small behavior changes at the narrowest responsible layer. Use when regression proof, preserved surrounding behavior, and task-relevant tests matter.
skill.summary: Create focused bug fixes with relevant regression proof and minimal impact on surrounding behavior.
skill.author: juliusbrussee

security_audit.summary: The single static finding is a false positive. The cited line limits unrelated code changes and does not request system reconnaissance or any dangerous action.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid cleanup, renaming, and abstraction outside fix.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 13 says to avoid cleanup, renaming, and unrelated abstraction. It contains no system reconnaissance instruction and instead restricts the scope of edits.

content.user_title: Fix Bugs with Focused, Verified Changes
content.value_statement: Broad fixes can introduce unrelated regressions and overwrite existing work. This skill traces each bug to its responsible layer and verifies a focused correction.
actual_capabilities: Reproduces a reported failure when practical or records the strongest available evidence.
Traces the observed symptom to the mechanism responsible for the incorrect behavior.
Changes the narrowest layer that owns the faulty behavior.
Preserves unrelated behavior and existing user changes.
Adds focused regression proof and runs the nearest affected validation gate.
limitations: It does not guarantee reproduction when the environment or required evidence is unavailable.
It does not perform unrelated cleanup, renaming, or architectural refactoring.
It depends on available tests and validation commands for regression proof.
It does not replace broader review for changes spanning multiple systems.

use_cases.title: Repair a Product Regression
use_cases.description: Trace a reported regression, correct its owning layer, and add focused proof without changing unrelated behavior.

use_cases.title: Review a Narrow Maintenance Fix
use_cases.description: Keep a maintenance patch limited to the defect while preserving existing user changes and nearby behavior.

use_cases.title: Stabilize a Failing Build
use_cases.description: Identify the mechanism behind a focused test failure and verify the smallest responsible correction.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Reproducible Bug
prompt_templates.prompt: Use surgical-patch to reproduce this bug, fix the narrowest responsible layer, and run the most relevant test: [bug details].
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has clear reproduction steps and needs a focused correction.

prompt_templates.title: Patch with Limited Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use surgical-patch for [symptom]. Capture the strongest available evidence, trace the cause, preserve unrelated behavior, and verify the focused fix.
prompt_templates.scenario: The failure is intermittent or difficult to reproduce directly.

prompt_templates.title: Protect Existing Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Fix [defect] with surgical-patch. Preserve current user modifications, avoid unrelated cleanup, and add only regression proof relevant to this defect.
prompt_templates.scenario: The working tree contains changes that must remain intact.

prompt_templates.title: Constrain a Cross-Layer Regression
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [regression] across affected layers. Patch only the layer owning the incorrect behavior, then run focused proof and the nearest affected gate.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced defect appears across several modules but requires a tightly scoped patch.

output_examples.input: The profile form clears the display name when only the avatar is updated.
output_examples.output: The update path now preserves an existing display name when that field is omitted. A focused regression test covers avatar-only updates.

output_examples.input: A parser accepts empty identifiers after the latest validation change.
output: Located the regression in identifier validation.
Restored rejection of empty identifiers without changing other parsing rules.
Ran the focused parser test and the nearest validation suite.

best_practices: Provide reproduction steps, expected behavior, and observed behavior whenever available.
Identify existing user changes that the patch must preserve.
Name the focused tests and validation gates relevant to the defect.
anti_patterns: Do not combine the bug fix with unrelated cleanup or renaming.
Do not request broad architectural changes when a responsible layer is already identifiable.
Do not treat a passing focused test as proof for unrelated system behavior.

faq.question: What types of tasks fit this skill?
faq.answer: It fits bug fixes and small behavior changes where minimal scope and regression proof are important.

faq.question: Does the skill always reproduce the failure first?
faq.answer: It reproduces the failure when practical. Otherwise, it captures the strongest evidence available before making a change.

faq.question: Will it refactor nearby code?
faq.answer: No. It avoids unrelated cleanup, renaming, and abstraction unless they are required to correct the behavior.

faq.question: How does it protect existing work?
faq.answer: It preserves unrelated behavior and user changes while limiting edits to the layer responsible for the defect.

faq.question: What validation does it perform?
faq.answer: It runs focused regression proof and the nearest affected test or validation gate available in the project.

faq.question: Can it handle large redesigns?
faq.answer: It is not intended for broad redesigns. Use it when the requested correction can remain narrow and independently verified.
